topStory.headline: College Board Survey: 74% of Faculty Report Student A.I. Use for Essays
topStory.summary:
A College Board research brief surveying more than 3,000 U.S. college faculty during summer 2025 reveals widespread concern about student A.I. use. According to the College Board, 74% of faculty report students using A.I. for essay and paper writing, while 67% observe students using it to paraphrase or rewrite content. Nearly half of faculty believe at least half their students use A.I. for writing tasks.

Faculty sentiment toward A.I. in higher education skews negative, with 45% holding an overall negative view compared to 34% positive. The survey found that 79% of faculty say they are just beginning to explore A.I. or need more guidance, with only 21% feeling confident in guiding student A.I. use. Meanwhile, 77% of faculty report personally using A.I. in their professional roles.

The research shows differences by institution type: faculty at more selective institutions report higher levels of student A.I. use and greater concern about academic impact, while faculty at open enrollment colleges are more likely to view A.I. as a practical instructional tool. Only 48% of respondents have formal classroom A.I. policies in place.

stories.headline: Faculty Moving Away From Outright A.I. Bans, UC Berkeley Study Finds
stories.summary: UC Berkeley researcher Igor Chirikov analyzed over 31,000 course syllabi from a large Texas university and found that highly restrictive A.I. policies introduced after ChatGPT's launch are being eased across disciplines, according to Inside Higher Ed. The exception is arts and humanities, which have maintained stricter policies. A.I. attribution requirements grew from 1% to 29% of syllabi between 2023 and 2025.

stories.headline: AAC&U Survey: 90% of Faculty Worry A.I. Will Diminish Critical Thinking
stories.summary: A survey of 1,057 faculty members by the American Association of Colleges and Universities and Elon University found that 90% believe A.I. will diminish students' critical thinking skills, according to Inside Higher Ed. Additionally, 95% expect overreliance on A.I. tools will increase. However, 61% also believe A.I. could improve and customize learning experiences.

stories.headline: Agentic A.I. Tool Designed to Complete Online Courses Draws Instructure Response
stories.summary: A 22-year-old entrepreneur who dropped out of Brown University launched Einstein, a tool that can autonomously log into Canvas, watch lectures, write papers, and submit assignments, according to Inside Higher Ed. The tool drew over 124,000 website visitors in three days before Canvas owner Instructure issued a cease-and-desist letter.
